text:
Anya Volkov: follow-up from today's incident where two hotstarts got wedged on streaming safetensors shards — one from a private registry that recently enabled gzip by default.
Daniel Kim: thanks — traces show the stream decoder waiting for an index marker that doesn't exist because the blob was an older safetensors layout.
Priya Nair: we keep iterating on probes & peek caches but I think we should consider a small on-disk/format-level change: add a 1-byte streamability flag into the safetensors header (v2) so loader can determine stream-safe at byte-0 without extra requests.
Marco Li: that would be neat. spec change pros: deterministic, zero-roundtrip detection, less edge-logic. cons: requires producers to republish or support dual-header.
Anya Volkov: exactly. proposal sketch: safetensors-v2 header: magic + version + flags. flags bit0 = streamable (index present at front), bit1 = compressed (gzip), bit2 = has-external-index. Old v1 files treated as "unknown" -> loader falls back to existing tiered probe (range/header/cache).
Daniel Kim: migration strategy: (A) require new model exports to default to v2, (B) add loader support for v2/v1 detection by reading first 64 bytes during open, (C) accept `x-rw-sf-version: v2` from registries to skip peek.
Priya Nair: backward compatibility: when loader sees v1 or unknown, use conservative index-first. Streaming allowed only if manifest `allow_streaming=true` for that model or registry is trusted. That avoids surprise OOM cascades.
Marco Li: implementation tasks: format PR for safetensors spec, exporter change (huggingface export tools + internal packager), loader read-first-64 patch, edge header support, and registry docs. Also add a compatibility shim that lets edge set `x-rw-sf-version` for proxies that can detect v2 on upload.
Anya Volkov: telemetry: emit `sf.header_version=v1|v2|unknown`, `sf.flags=bitmask`, `decision=stream|index`, `probe.method=None|range|head|manifest`. Dashboard: percent v2 by registry, stream-decision-failure-rate.
Daniel Kim: test plan: unit header parse, cross-version roundtrip tests, integration with gzipped v2 files, and stress test with concurrent hotstarts to validate no extra HEAD/range QPS.
Priya Nair: runbook: how to force index-first, how to set manifest `allow_streaming`, how to interpret `sf.header_version=unknown` alerts. Also add rollback steps for enabling v2 enforcement.
Marco Li: rollout plan: (1) implement loader detection + telemetry (1 sprint), (2) land exporter change + edge header (1 sprint), (3) announce registry migration and provide a conversion tool (CLI) for partners (1 sprint), (4) canary: 1% Dedicated for 2 weeks, monitor decision=fallback and hotstart latency.
Anya Volkov: infra-bot: please file a tracking issue and assign owners.
infra-bot: created ISSUE-ML-4422: "safetensors-v2 header + streamability flag + loader migration" assigned to Anya Volkov, Daniel Kim, Marco Li, Priya Nair. ETA: 3 sprints.
Daniel Kim: compatibility note: some internal checkpoints are immutable; exporters should be able to publish a small sidecar containing the v2 header (first 64b) to registries so loaders can consult without republishing full checkpoint. That lets us adopt faster.
Priya Nair: nice idea — sidecar named `<model>.sft.meta` with first-64-bytes and signature. registry can serve it at predictable URL; loader consults it as cheapest option. add `x-rw-sf-sidecar: available` header when present.
Marco Li: security: sidecar should be signed to avoid rogue registries lying about streamability. include checksum and sig; loader verifies against model manifest fingerprint.
Anya Volkov: ok agreed. add tasks: sidecar spec, signing format, loader sidecar lookup + verification, and runbook updates.
Daniel Kim: I'll draft the safetensors-v2 spec and sidecar proto. Marco can do signing doc and Priya the loader changes & telemetry.
Priya Nair: I'll open the loader PR sketch today with decision defaults: v2+streamable => stream; v2+compressed => index-first unless manifest allows streaming; v1/unknown => conservative index-first.
Marco Li: test matrix includes a chaos test where sidecar lies (mismatched checksum) to confirm loader rejects and falls back.
Anya Volkov: thanks all — this feels like a stronger long-term fix compared to ad-hoc probes. Sync on RFC PR thread. :shipit:
